newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-GOVERNMENT TO INVESTIGATE SOUTH AFRICAN RUGBY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GOVERNMENT TO INVESTIGATE SOUTH AFRICAN RUGBY.

text.p: The South African sports ministry has set up a three-man task force to investigate the affairs of rugby union in the country.
The team begins its work on Friday when it will look into issues including alleged financial irregularities in the sport's administration.
"There is substance in these allegations," sports minister Mr Steve Tshwete was quoted as saying in a Johannesburg newspaper on Saturday.
"We now want to establish the authenticity or otherwise of the allegations."

The ministry was presented with a dossier of "evidence" detailing alleged mis-management with the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) by Johannesburg accountant Brian van Rooyen. He has never publicly detailed his charges.

Van Rooyen revealed the existence of the dossier after he made an unsuccessful attempt to unseat the all-powerful SARFU president Louis Luyt from his position as chairman as Transvaal Rugby Union last October.
Tshwete said the inquiry had also been prompted by concerns expressed in parliament and elsewhere.
"I want a process to purge rugby of any negative profile and I don't want it to drag on," said Tshwete.
The investigators will examine rugby's administration as well as the development programme, professionalism, ownership of stadiums and television deals.
SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer, son-in-law of Luyt, said: "We have nothing to hide. We offered to allow auditors to examine our books and the offer still stands.

A commission of inquiry into the running of the South African Football Association (SAFA) ordered by Tshwete uncovered "gross misconduct" and led to the resignation of SAFA president Stix Morewa earlier this year.
Tshwete and his team will meet SARFU's executive committee on Friday. The investigation is expected to take two months.
